conviction_note: The top line is already pre-announced ($127m H1, $360m FY reaffirmed on 2026-08-06), so the only genuinely new information on 1 September is gross margin, cash and the balance sheet - and every independent document I could reach on those three points reads worse than the narrative the +16.8% five-day run-up is built on; sized at -4.5 rather than deeper because 15% of float is short, front-expiry open interest is 4:1 calls, and this management runs a promotional call with an Oct 6 Nasdaq Investor Day already teed up.

findings.finding: Reward Loyalty UK Limited (CH 10701520), the business Rezolve bought for $239,557,869 cash on 2026-02-10 and told US investors would add 'approximately $90 million of EBITDA-accretive revenue', filed audited group accounts at Companies House on 2026-07-25 for its year ended 30 April 2025 showing turnover of GBP 52.89m (approx $67-71m) and gross profit of about GBP 21m - i.e. a ~40% gross-margin business generating roughly GBP 2m EBITDA on 186-209 employees, not a 90%-margin software asset. [snippet_only: the 74-page PDF is behind an S3 redirect WebFetch cannot follow; figures are from two independent CH aggregators reading the same filing]
findings.why_not_priced: This is the single largest component of Rezolve's revenue ramp and its real economics exist only in a UK private-company filing made five weeks ago, in GBP, on an April year-end, under a name no US screen maps to RZLV. If the market had it, the Feb 2026 deal would not have been sold to a US audience as 'non-dilutive' and 'EBITDA-accretive $90m revenue' without pushback, Cantor would not be carrying Overweight on a 90%-software-margin frame, and the front-expiry chain would not be 4:1 calls at a 0.25 put/call OI ratio. It also creates a two-sided trap on 1 September: consolidate Reward gross and consolidated gross margin collapses; consolidate net and the $360m guide loses ~$30m of its base.
findings.independence: Independently corroborated by Endole reading the same 2026-07-25 filing (turnover GBP 52.89m, net assets GBP 5.99m, total liabilities GBP 57.83m, 209 employees) at https://open.endole.co.uk/insight/company/10701520-reward-loyalty-uk-limited . Cross-checks against finding 2 (the SEC-side gross-margin arithmetic) and against Rezolve's own $90m claim at https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/10/3235266/0/en/Rezolve-Ai-PLC-Expands-Core-AI-Commerce-Platform-with-Acquisition-of-Reward-Loyalty-UK-Limited.html . The Companies House filing history establishing the 2026-07-25 group accounts (and that they were filed ~6 months past the 31 Jan 2026 statutory deadline) is at https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/10701520/filing-history

findings.finding: Rezolve's consolidated gross margin has already fallen from the 95.8% it reported for H1 2025 to 66.0% for audited FY2025 (revenue $46,800,099 less cost of revenue $15,922,202 per the 20-F income statement), which implies roughly 61% in H2 2025 - and H1 2026 is the FIRST period that consolidates Reward at all, on top of Crownpeak (from 1 Dec 2025) and GroupBy. The 1 September interims are the first gross-margin disclosure the market will see since the 95.8% print.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody previews an FPI's semi-annual gross margin - there is no 10-Q, no quarterly cadence, and the baseline records n=0 recoverable earnings reactions on EDGAR, so there is no sell-side model of this line to be wrong about. The market's live anchor is the 95.8% H1 2025 figure, which was reported as a beat against a 60-70% analyst expectation, plus the company's own August 2026 assertion of 'core software margins above 90%' in its Commerce.com exchange-offer material. If a 40-point margin compression were priced, RZLV would not have added 16.8% in five sessions into the print and the 25-delta chain would show put demand rather than a 0.25 put/call OI ratio.
findings.independence: The 95.8% H1 2025 gross margin and the 60-70% analyst expectation are from a separate source, the coverage of the H1 2025 interim 6-K, at https://www.investing.com/news/sec-filings/rezolve-ai-files-interim-financial-statements-for-first-half-of-2025-93CH-4267350 [snippet_only]. Mechanically this is the SEC-side confirmation of finding 1, reached from a different document set.

findings.finding: Both of Rezolve AI PLC's registered charges are still shown as OUTSTANDING at Companies House - Monroe Capital Management Advisors LLC (charge created 2025-12-22) and Crownpeak Technology Holdings LLC (created 2026-01-19) - covering the $101,540,086 Monroe borrowing that the 20-F classified as SHORT-TERM debt at 31 Dec 2025 and the $50,000,000 Crownpeak promissory notes, while no 6-K filed in 2026 announces any refinancing, and the 20-F's going-concern mitigation depended explicitly on 'refinancing short-term debt'. Cash arithmetic: $111,112,251 at 31 Dec 2025, plus the ~$250m registered direct raise closed 2026-01-21 (62.5m shares at $4, ~5% placement fee), less the $239,557,869 cash paid for Reward on 2026-02-10, leaves roughly $110m before any H1 operating burn (FY2025 operating burn was $63,147,255 on a far smaller cost base). The 1 September interims are the first balance sheet since 31 Dec 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: Going concern is in the wire from the March 20-F, but the resolution of a $101.5m current maturity is not: the marginal holder has been given nine 6-Ks since June about India, a payments partner, the World Cup, watermarking, Google and Commerce.com, and not one about debt. The charge register is the only public place the security status is visible and it is a UK filing, not an SEC one. If the market had priced a cash-versus-current-debt squeeze, a 15%-of-float short base would not be facing a 0.25 put/call OI ratio and the stock would not have run 16.8% into a first-balance-sheet-in-eight-months event. The burn estimate is my arithmetic and flagged as such; the four dollar figures are each sourced.
findings.independence: Debt composition and short/long split from the 20-F schedule at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920294/000119312526132456/R73.htm ; balance sheet at .../R2.htm ; FY2025 operating cash outflow at .../R8.htm ; the $239,557,869 Reward consideration and the 2026-01-20 issue of 62.5m shares at $4 at .../R111.htm ; the absence of any 2026 6-K on financing is verifiable from https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001920294.json

findings.finding: The entire +16.8% five-day run-up in the baseline is one company-issued press release: 'Google Selects Rezolve Ai's Proprietary Distributed Database Platform' on 2026-08-25, which moved the stock ~19% in a session (close 2.43 on 08-24, pre-market 2.645 on 08-25) and which discloses no contract value, no term, no revenue and no Google quote or spokesperson; Google's own Blockchain Analytics / Web3 documentation and partner blogs name Subsquid and Chainstack for exactly this function and do not mention Rezolve; and Rezolve did not furnish the release on a Form 6-K, its last 6-K being 2026-08-06.
findings.why_not_priced: The market has priced this as a hard commercial win - a 19% single-session repricing of a $1.1bn market cap is ~$210m of value ascribed to an announcement carrying zero disclosed economics. The 1 September call is the first forum where management must either quantify it inside the $360m guide or decline to. The sweep's brief attributes the run-up to the 2026-08-06 revenue pre-announcement, which is arithmetically impossible for a five-day window, so even the baseline's own reading of what is priced is wrong here. Note the immediately prior promotional release (2026-08-18, World Cup scale metrics) drew a -5.94% reaction, which is the fade pattern this name actually has.
findings.independence: Google-side absence checked directly against Google's own documentation at https://docs.cloud.google.com/blockchain-analytics/docs/supported-datasets and the Google Cloud Web3 partner posts; the day-by-day price path and the 08-18 reaction are from a different source at https://stockstotrade.com/news/rezolve-ai-plc-rzlv-news-2026_08_25/ . Independent of findings 1-3, which are accounting rather than narrative.

findings.finding: The reaffirmed ~$360m FY2026 guide requires H2 2026 revenue of ~$233m against ~$127m in H1, +83% half-on-half, at a point where the acquired run-rates are largely already in the base: Reward at GBP 52.89m/yr (~$67-71m), Crownpeak at ~$70m/yr for an $81.0m purchase price, GroupBy at ~$30m/yr - about $84m per half combined - leaving roughly $149m of H2 from everything else versus roughly $43m in H1.
findings.why_not_priced: The halves arithmetic ($127m and $360m) is derivable from the 2026-08-06 wire and I assume it is priced; the part that is not is the acquired-revenue denominator, which needs Reward's actual GBP turnover from a Companies House filing rather than the $90m the US market was given. I am sizing this small precisely because most of it IS in the wire - it is a decomposition, not a discovery, and it earns a small number.
findings.independence: Overlaps finding 1 directly (same Reward number). Crownpeak's $81.0m price and ~$70m revenue and GroupBy's ~$30m are from Rezolve's own filings and deal coverage; the $127m / $360m pair is from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000119312526338451/rzlv-ex99_1.htm

searched_and_found_nothing: Any Google or Google Cloud confirmation of the 2026-08-25 selection on Google's own domains (cloud.google.com, blog.google, docs.cloud.google.com) - absence only, not disproof; Google's named partners for blockchain data pipelines into BigQuery are Subsquid and Chainstack
Any 6-K, 424B5 or F-3/A in 2026 disclosing a Monroe refinancing, extension, waiver or repayment - EDGAR shows nothing between 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-31 except the Form 4 and 13D/A

The Form 4 and SCHEDULE 13D/A filed 2026-08-28, three days before the print - read both; they are housekeeping (a 2018-vintage call option exercised by Bradley Wickens at $1.48 over 1,566,697 shares, a second over 2,025,496 shares expired, a 543,993-share estate distribution to DBLP), Item 4 states no present plans, no open-market buying or selling by Wagner. No insider signal.

Trade receivables / DSO for H1 2026 - not obtainable; the 2026-04-30 Q1 6-K carried a press release only, with no interim balance sheet, so 31 Dec 2025 (AR and unbilled $39,176,319 on $46.8m revenue) is the last data point in existence

The 74-page Reward Loyalty UK group accounts PDF itself - Companies House 302-redirects to a signed S3 URL that WebFetch cannot follow, and Endole/CompanyCheck/Pomanda all return 403; figures are aggregator snippets of that filing and are marked snippet_only

Revenue customer-concentration note in the FY2025 20-F - the AR concentration table (R59) is populated for 2024 (La Liga 100%, Servicios Liverpool 17%) and blank for 2025, so no read on who is behind the ramp

The 'Other Digital Assets, net $16,373,705' Level 2 balance and $102,801 crypto intangibles - real and odd for a claimed SaaS company, but too small to size and I could not establish whether any revenue was settled in tokens

The unexplained '1 Month Ended Dec 31 2025' revenue of $19,419,993 on the face of the 20-F income statement (41% of full-year FY2025 revenue in one dimensioned month) - could not determine whether this is a Crownpeak stub-period disclosure or a December licence spike, so I did not size it

Whether the Commerce.com (CMRC) exchange offer escalates on the 1 September call - the offer is live (425 filed 2026-08-06, CMRC board rejected and adopted a rights plan) but I found no evidence of a formal exchange offer launch being imminent
Glassdoor/LinkedIn/job-posting evidence of contraction against the '550 India specialists' claim - nothing usable found
baseline_tension: Everything I found cuts against the baseline's priced state rather than agreeing with it: the baseline records a +16.8% five-day run-up, a 0.25 put/call open-interest ratio (call-skewed positioning), no usable skew, and n=0 reaction history, i.e. a price that has absorbed the pre-announced $127m/$360m headline and then added ~19% for an unquantified Google press release - while the three documents nobody in the US chain has read (Reward's GBP 52.89m turnover and ~40% gross margin at Companies House, Rezolve's still-outstanding Monroe and Crownpeak charges, and the 66.0% audited FY2025 gross margin against a 95.8% H1 2025 anchor) all point the same way on the only lines that are actually new on 1 September; the honest offset is that a 15%-of-float short base and a promotional call with an Oct 6 Nasdaq Investor Day queued up can overwhelm a balance sheet for one session, which is why -4.5 sits well inside the 12.04% implied move.
